newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia parliament resumes debate on PM.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia parliament resumes debate on PM.

text.p: Rightwing leaders denounced a defector in Slovenia's parliament on Thursday but a vote later in the day was expected to give the centre-left's Janez Drnovsek another term as prime minister.

"Counting on one vote of a man who can betray basic moral principles does not lead to a reliable government," declared Christian Democrat Lojze Peterle, who was Slovenia's first prime minister after independence from Yugoslavia.
Leaders of the conservative People's Party, centre-right Social Democrats and Christian Democrats, said they would not support a new Drnovsek administration.
"This government's results are always the same -- ever bigger social differences and an ever increasing number of unemployed and marginalised," said Joze Zagozen of the People's Party.
November's election left Slovenia with a hung parliament in which Drnovsek's Liberal Democrats and their allies had 45 of the 90 votes.
The opposition's hopes of power were swept away on Wednesday when Ciril Pucko defected from the Christian Democrats and promised Drnovsek the one-vote margin he needs.
The newspaper Dnevnik reported that police provided special security for Pucko's family because of threats since his defection.
